newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO ADDS TO BARCELONA INJURY WOES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO ADDS TO BARCELONA INJURY WOES.

text.p: Despite having one of the strongest squads in world football, Barcelona coach Bobby Robson finds himself struggling to put together a team for the vital Spanish league clash with champions Atletico Madrid.
With three Portuguese players away on international duty, Robson must also reckon without injured Bulgarian striker Hristo Stoichkov and Brazilian prodigy Ronaldo.
Club doctors said on Thursday that the 20-year old Ronaldo had aggravated a stretched muscle in his left leg in the Cup Winners' Cup match at Red Star Belgrade last week.
Ronaldo, who will also miss Brazil's friendly against Cameroon next Thursday, will be replaced by Spanish international striker Juan Pizzi.

Meanwhile, Barcelona's second reserve keeper Julen Lopetegui is definitely out with a finger injury, leaving no obvious substitute for Carlos Busquets -- who will take over between the posts in the absence of Vitor Baia.
Robson will also have to fight pressure from club directors not to call up the obvious replacement for Stoichkov, left-sided striker Angel Cuellar.
Under Spanish league rules, Cuellar would no longer be able to move to another club if he plays another game before the country's transfer market reopens in December.
With a move back to Real Betis already on the cards for Cuellar, Barcelona are unlikely to put at risk the sale of a player who spent most of last season injured and who has failed to impress Robson.
With right-sided striker Luis Figo also out, Robson may have to call upon the Garcia brothers, Oscar and Roger, or even midfielder Robert Prosinecki of Croatia.
A set-piece specialist, Prosinecki has struggled to find his form since joining Real Madrid after winning the European Cup with Red Star Belgrade in 1991.
After moving to Oviedo on loan, Prosinecki signed for Barcelona last season but has once again failed to settle and is now tipped to go to Sevilla.
The big doubt for Atletico is another Balkan free-kick expert, Milinko Pantic.
The Serb is still suffering pains in his right knee after a collision in last Sunday's 3-0 win over Oviedo but has said that he is keen to play in the Camp Nou.

Pantic's monopoly of dead-ball situations leaves Atletico without an obvious replacement in an area which is a major source of goals for the side. Defender Toni Munoz and striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider would be the most obvious candidates to take over in Pantic's absence.
Always one to have a go, Pantic scored a superb goal from a seemingly impossible angle against Borussia Dortmund in the European Champions' League.

It is in the premier continental competition that Atletico have shown their best form this season, although consecutive league victories have led coach Radomir Antic to claim that his team is back at last season's peak.
Barcelona, by contrast, have struggled to reproduce their domestic form in Europe.

But it was in the home leg of the Cup Winner's Cup tie against Red Star Belgrade that Barcelona proved that they could at least function without Ronaldo, as another Brazilian, Giovanni, took over to lead his side to a 3-1 victory.
